'''''Orchis anthropophora''''' (formerly '''''Aceras anthropophorum'''''), the '''man orchid''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a [[Europe]]an species of [[orchid]] whose flowers resemble a human figure. The head is formed by the [[petal]]s and [[sepal]]s, and the suspended torso and limbs by the lobes of the [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]]. It usually grows in [[calcareous grassland]].

== Description ==
The man orchid is a [[herbaceous perennial]], growing to a height of {{Convert|20|to|40|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}}. A basal rosette of {{Convert|5|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} lanceolate leaves develops from a [[tuber]] {{Convert|6|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} in diameter, and between April and June a central flower spike is produced bearing up to fifty small, stemless flowers – the flowers vary from greenish, with a yellow-green labellum, to green, streaked and marked with purple. 
[[Image:Aceras anthropophorum leaves.jpg|thumb|left|Leaf rosette before flowering]]
[[Image:Aceras anthropophora (detail).jpg|left|thumb]]

==Habitat==
''Orchis anthropophora'' favours moderately sunny meadows on well-drained, often [[calcareous]] soil. It is to be found around the [[Mediterranean]] area, and in central and western [[Europe]] as far north as southern [[England]]. It also grows in [[Alpine climate|alpine]] areas, but not at high altitude.

It is native to Great Britain, central Europe (Austria, Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, and Switzerland), southwestern Europe (the Balearic Islands, Corsica, France, Portugal, Sardinia, and Spain), southeastern Europe (Albania, Greece, Italy, Crete, Sicily, and countries of the former Yugoslavia), northern Africa (Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia), and western Asia (Cyprus, East Aegean Islands, Lebanon, Syria, and Turkey).<ref name="WCSP_142231"/>
